name: freesave-read-swapped
description:
FREESAVE, THE THIRD ARM — the SILENT one, and the class doc 41 actually warns about. The same .sav and the same no-input timeline as the other two reads, against a build whose SaveBlock1 layout changed while its SIZE did not: four bytes taken off filler1 at 0x988 and handed back at the end of the struct. sizeof(struct SaveBlock1) is 15568 in both builds, so every one of the fourteen sectors keeps its size, every checksum is recomputed over the same length it was written with, and the save is ACCEPTED — while flags[], vars[], dexSeen and dexCaught have all slid 4 bytes down.

This arm exists because the FREE_* switches CANNOT produce this case. Every one of them changes a struct size, and freesave-read-flipped.json showed the engine catches every size change and wipes. A layout change that keeps the size is the one the engine has no defence against at all.

The `_oldpos` probes are what turn 'wrong' into a measurement: they read where each seeded byte still physically sits, so the run shows the data present and the field looking four bytes away from it. Every one of them is an exact non-zero value, which is the discriminating class.
symbols_from_why: gFreeSaveHookLatch and gFreeSaveOffsets are fork-only symbols.

probes.why: THE CLAIM. Predicted SAVE_STATUS_OK == 1 — the same value the control gets, on a build that reads the file wrong.
BELOW THE CUT, unmoved at 0x234. Predicted 1, exactly as the control.
This build's FLAG_SYS_POKEDEX_GET byte: flags[] moved to 4716, so 4716+268 = 4984. It reads whatever lived at 4984 in the writing build — four bytes earlier in flags[], i.e. someone else's flags.
4988 — where the seeded byte physically is, and still is. Predicted 2.
This build's VAR_RECYCLE_GOODS: vars[] moved to 5016, so 5016+64 = 5080.
5084 — the seeded 0x5AA5, four bytes from where this build's vars[] looks for it.
13849 — the writing build's dexCaught byte 0. Predicted 255, still there.
CONTROL. SaveBlock2 is untouched by this edit, so this must still read 7 — which is what proves the damage is confined to the block whose layout moved.
CONTROL. Cold CPU start, and no Sav2_ClearSetDefault this time — the status never reaches the branch that wipes.

assert.why: THE WHOLE POINT. SAVE_STATUS_OK — byte-for-byte the control's verdict, on a build that cannot read the file correctly. Contrast freesave-read-flipped, which returns 2 for a change the engine CAN see.
Below the cut, so genuinely correct here. It is what makes the arm dangerous rather than obviously broken: the game loads, the party is real, the save says OK.
THE MEASUREMENT. The seeded flag byte is present in RAM, at the offset the OLD build put it. Exact non-zero, discriminating class.
0x5AA5 at 5084, four bytes from where this build's vars[] reads. A second, independently seeded field saying the same thing.
The dexCaught byte, present at the old offset — and this one is in sector 4, whose size did NOT change here, which is exactly why it survived when the flipped arm lost it.
CONTROL, exact non-zero. SaveBlock2's layout was not touched, so it reads correctly — the damage is confined to the block that moved, not spread by the mere fact of a mismatched build.
